This release updates the bundled Elise core to **1.0.3** and fixes Hysteria2 bandwidth negotiation, TCP sniffing delays, and UDP interoperability using V2bX's Go implementation as the reference.

- Use paced Brutal congestion control when the client specifies a receive rate, capped by the panel's server transmit limit; use BBR when the rate is unknown or client bandwidth is ignored.
- Convert panel Mbps values to protocol bytes per second correctly, preserve unlimited bandwidth semantics, and honor `ignore_client_bandwidth` across panel adapters.
- Keep enough packets in flight on short-RTT connections to avoid delayed-ACK stalls while maintaining the negotiated pacing rate. Loss compensation is bounded to 25% and uses Quinn's byte-based samples.
- Send TCP acceptance before domain sniffing so clients waiting for the response can supply application data. Preserve sniffed audit rules and avoid sending a second response after an early acceptance.
- Support UDP replies to Hysteria clients that omit the datagram transport parameter in Chrome-style handshakes, including fragmented messages.
- Split kernel-coalesced obfuscated UDP packets before decoding each salt, and request larger kernel socket buffers subject to OS limits.
- Preserve the original authenticated user and bandwidth settings when authentication is retried on an existing connection.

Validation: 308 Elise tests, 306 QUIC tests, and installer contract checks passed. An interoperability test using the Hysteria v2.12.2 Go client verifies concurrent TCP, sniffed blocking rules, fragmented UDP, Salamander, and five bandwidth/obfuscation modes. Formatting passed and Clippy completed with existing warnings.

In local testing, a concurrent 1 MiB transfer plus UDP roundtrips took about 1.13 seconds at an 8 Mbps server transmit limit, with and without Salamander. This is a local pacing check, not a production-network benchmark.

The release includes V2bX Linux amd64, arm64, and s390x archives, plus Elise Linux amd64 and arm64 archives with SHA-256 checksums.

To update an existing Elise installation, run `v2bx elise install v0.6.8`. The installer verifies the archive checksum, restarts active Elise instances, and restores the previous binary if restart checks fail. Active sessions may disconnect during the restart.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/phungvanquy/v2bx-new/compare/v0.6.7...v0.6.8)
